text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD-2431 triggered for service=redwood-inference-api - p99 latency breach in eu-west2. Auto-runbook started.

alice (oncall): grabbing. seeing p95 ~ 820ms -> 1.1s, p99 ~ 3.7s -> 5.2s for generation endpoint. Streaming stalls spiking, clients reporting partial frames.

carol (sre): confirm dashboards — tail spikes started ~ 1858201200. Error rate stable but tcp retransmits up, TLS handshake latency high. Looks like cross-AZ path.

bob (neteng): I'm seeing increased SYN->ACK times on flows going through NAT-gw-eu-west2-b. Packet drops on forward path plus high conntrack counts. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion on that NAT.

gcp-nat-alert-bot: GCP NAT metrics: ephemeral_ports_in_use=46785/49152 (95%), conntrack_drops=2300 in last 5m for nat-gw-eu-west2-b.

alice (oncall): customer impact: multiple high-throughput customers show streaming stalls (clients time out at 30s), several support tickets opened. Need mitigation ASAP.

dan (cs): flagged priority customers: AcornGames (paying Dedicated), OrionSearch (hosted). Orion is reporting user-facing lag, CS on call is escalated.

frank (runtime): if TLS handshakes are slow, KV cache warmups will be impacted and tail tokens will stall. We should route to alternate NAT / AZ and reduce new TLS sessions where possible.

bob (neteng): mitigation options:
- increase NAT ephemeral port pool (if allowed) / create additional NAT gateway in eu-west2-a
- re-route egress from eu-west2-b to eu-west2-a via route table change (fast but riskier)
- enable connection pooling on upstream egress (temporary)

alice (oncall): please do simple action first: stand up second NAT in eu-west2-a and failover traffic. Eve, can infra create a new NAT and attach to subnet?

eve (infra): creating nat-gw-eu-west2-a-2 now. provisioning.. ETA ~ 90s. updating SNAT rules to prefer nat-a once ready.

carol (sre): while infra provisions, flip routing for low-risk customer tests (canary). frank, can runtime route a subset of requests (5%) to eu-west2-a? We want sampling before full shift.

frank (runtime): yes — adding weight rule in smart-router: model-route=generate-prod -> prefer eu-west2-a weight 5%. Patch pushed: 
```
route update generate-prod --weight eu-west2-a=5
```
Confirming traffic started hitting nat-a.

(90s later)

eve (infra): nat-gw-eu-west2-a-2 ready and in route table. Health checks OK.

bob (neteng): conntrack counts on nat-a low; SYN latencies for sample traffic down by ~60%. p95 now 420ms for canary.

alice (oncall): ok ramp to 50% for non-critical traffic, keep 0% for Dedicated/reserved customers until we confirm. frank, can you do that?

frank (runtime): ramping to 50% for guest/hosted. running: 
```
route update generate-prod --weight eu-west2-a=50
```
Monitoring streaming stalls and p99.

(10m later)

carol (sre): metrics: overall p95 dropped from ~1.1s -> 420ms, p99 from 5.2s -> 1.4s. Streaming stalls reduced 78% in affected customers. conntrack_drops on old nat down to near zero.

alice (oncall): good. escalate next steps: 1) keep nat-a active 2) schedule permanent NAT capacity increase or autoscale 3) add connection health metrics to alerting (conntrack_drops > 100 in 5m) 4) postmortem.

bob (neteng): root cause likely combination: surge in short-lived TLS connections from a few high-throughput customers + lower-than-expected ephemeral port pool due to recent routing change that consolidated egress in eu-west2-b. Also DNS retries seemed amplified because of TTL change in our internal resolver — more concurrent attempts to external hosts.

frank (runtime): interesting note: our runtime opens fresh upstream connections for model_fetch on each request for certain config (keepalive disabled). We'll push a quick config change to enable connection reuse for downstream model repo fetches to reduce handshake churn.

eve (infra): I'll file infra task: increase ephemeral port quota and enable NAT autoscale where supported. Also we'll add a dedicated NAT for high-throughput tenants (Dedicated customers) to isolate impact.

dan (cs): updated customers: CS reached out to AcornGames and OrionSearch — both saw degradation but confirm service restored. Shared immediate mitigation and ETA for permanent fix. No data loss.

alice (oncall): handoff: I need to go offline for a 30m blocker. @carol you're SRE lead until I return. Keep paging on any regression.

carol (sre): ack taking over. logging action items in incident tracker. current state: mitigated, rolling NAT split, monitoring for regression for 1h.

bob (neteng): creating follow-up ticket NET-512: Evaluate egress consolidation change, add capacity guardrails.

frank (runtime): PR with keepalive changes: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/842 - toggles keepalive for model fetches (default on). Rolling patch to 30% to validate.

alice (oncall): returning. thanks team. final checklist before close:
- infra: confirm NAT autoscale or manual capacity increase (eve)
- neteng: guardrails and alert tweaks (bob)
- runtime: keepalive default change + canary (frank)
- sre: postmortem draft with timeline & customer impact (carol)
- cs: customer comms summary (dan)

carol (sre): will draft postmortem. brief timeline for postmortem intro:
- 1858201200: p95/p99 drift observed
- 1858202000: PagerDuty PD-2431 triggered
- 1858202100: oncall paged, initial triage (alice)
- 1858202400: infra provision started for nat-a
- 1858202600: canary traffic to nat-a (5%)
- 1858202800: ramp to 50% - metrics improved
- 1858203300: routing stable, dedicated customers kept on isolated path
- 1858203700: incident declared mitigated, monitoring

alice (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. keeping watch for 60m. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

carol (sre): postmortem link will go to #incidents when ready. closing thread for now.

(annotations: no title field per slack thread policy)
